---
title: "IntroStatGPT"
description: "Using AI tools for the statistical computing in this course"
---

IntroStatGPT is how we do statistical computing in this course. You ask for a
table, a graph, or a model fit in ordinary language; ChatGPT's Codex runs R
behind the scenes and hands back the output, ready to check and drop into a
report. You never write code from scratch, and you are evaluated on concepts,
not code. What you still own is the important part: choosing the method,
checking the output, and deciding what it means.

## Start here

1. [Install and set up IntroStatGPT](introstatgpt/setup.qmd) — do this once,
   before you first use it. Activate your UT ChatGPT account, install R and the
   ChatGPT desktop app, download the IntroStatGPT folder, and run the setup.
2. [Use IntroStatGPT](introstatgpt/use.qmd) — the everyday workflow: find the
   available data, request an analysis, revise it, browse the gallery, organize
   your outputs, and compile a Word report.
3. [Working with IntroStatGPT and Codex](introstatgpt/working.qmd) — how to
   make requests that produce checkable output, how to check it, and what to
   save.

## Download

[IntroStatGPT_intensive.zip](files/IntroStatGPT_intensive.zip) (13 MB) — the
folder the setup page asks you to extract. It contains the IntroStatGPT setup
and the course datasets.

Your ability to complete any assignment, quiz, or exam never depends on an AI
tool working: known-good tables and figures are provided alongside every
assignment, and you can use them to check your own output or instead of it.
